stories.headline: Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace injured: What's next for the OKC Thunder?
stories.summary: The Thunder will be without two starting guards for months. Could they make a trade to try to replace Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace?
stories.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder lost two starters to long-term injuries in their 108-101 win over the LA Clippers on Sunday night.

General manager Sam Presti announced Monday that guard Jalen Williams will undergo surgery for a dislocated left ankle and fractured fibula, while guard Cason Wallace will undergo surgery for a torn labrum in his left shoulder. Both players are expected to miss several months.

Williams was placed on a stretcher and wheeled off the court after he was injured on a drive to the basket late in the fourth quarter. Wallace left the game in the first quarter and didn't return.

They're both big losses for the Thunder, who were counting on Williams to get back to his All-Star form from the 2024-25 season and Wallace to step into the starting lineup. Williams missed 49 regular-season games last season while recovering from surgery on his right wrist and then injuring both hamstrings. He played in just five games -- and 107 total minutes -- in the postseason as OKC was beaten by the San Antonio Spurs in seven games in the Western Conference finals. Wallace signed a five-year, $139 million contract extension just before the season began.

How bad do these injuries hurt the Thunder, who are 3-0 and believe they have the talent to make it back to the NBA Finals? Do they have flexibility to make a move to replace Williams or Wallace? ESPN's reporters and analysts weigh in:

What was the early word on Williams' injury inside the Thunder?
Emotional devastation, as evidenced by Shai Gilgeous-Alexander tearing up on the court.

It's gut-wrenching any time a player suffers a gruesome injury, but hearts are especially heavy for Williams in Oklahoma City. This is a young star who has had horrific injury luck despite doing everything right in terms of conditioning and rehab.

Williams' performance during the 2025 title run -- toughing it out with a shooting wrist that required surgery and still delivering 40 points in pivotal Game 5 of the NBA Finals -- will always be legendary in Oklahoma City. His injury misfortune has been miserable since with recurring hamstring strains that robbed him of most of last season and this cruel twist a week into this season.

The Thunder are a tight-knit team that has had to deal with the emotional consequences that come with the business of basketball. It stung to see title-winning teammates Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins traded in salary-slashing deals. This injury causes a deeper pain that the Thunder will have to process while figuring out how to fill a massive hole in the lineup. -- Tim MacMahon

How big of a hole will these losses leave for Oklahoma City?
These two injuries are the most important development of the new season's first week in terms of how they change the championship picture. The Thunder still have excellent depth and star power at the guard and center positions, but they already shed a fair amount of perimeter depth over the summer by trading Dort, Wiggins and Joe. Without Williams in particular, they're now perilously thin on the wing.

Williams' absence hurts the Thunder on offense -- his unavailability might well have prevented the Thunder from scoring enough to beat the Spurs in the playoffs last season -- but at least they still have Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain supporting two-time MVP Gilgeous-Alexander on that end. The larger problem comes on defense, which is the core of the Thunder's identity. They've led the league in defensive rating in each of the past two seasons and rank second thus far in 2026-27.

Last season, the Thunder had four perimeter players who were recent All-Defensive honorees. Trading Dort removed one of them, and the injuries to Williams and Wallace remove two more. For now, that series of unfortunate events leaves only Alex Caruso among the Thunder's elite perimeter defenders, and Oklahoma City prefers to load-manage him throughout the season to keep him fresh for the postseason. (Caruso has averaged 18.8 minutes per game in the regular season with the Thunder, versus 24.1 in the playoffs.)

Even if Wallace can return from his torn labrum for the postseason, he's smaller and less physically stout than either Dort or Williams, which could create significant problems as the Thunder contend with the other top teams in the West. In the postseason, they'll need to defend some combination of De'Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle; LaMelo Ball and Anthony Edwards; Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves; and Amen Thompson and Kevin Durant. Caruso can't guard them all.

Moreover, the simultaneous injuries to Williams and Wallace further eat away at Oklahoma City's margin of error, which had been meaningfully reduced by the team's summer trades. The new season is just three games old, and more injuries are probably coming -- but the Thunder can't afford to suffer more because their roster depth isn't as strong as it was a year or two ago. -- Zach Kram

How much flexibility do the Thunder have to make a move?
Oklahoma City will likely receive a $15 million disabled player exception. The exception would allow the team to sign or trade for a player in the last year of his contract. Using more than $6.9 million, however, would cause the Thunder to exceed the second apron. They are not hard-capped and can go past the threshold.

Besides the potential disabled player exception, Oklahoma City also has three large trade exceptions: $17.8 million, $11.3 million and $9.2 million. The Thunder are allowed to use the trade exception and still exceed the second apron.

The McCain trade last season showed their willingness to add to their roster during the regular season.

Oklahoma City has seven tradeable first-round picks -- including three in the 2027 draft -- and 21 second-rounders available. -- Bobby Marks

Are there any natural targets available for OKC to pursue?
As Bobby notes, Oklahoma City's financial situation will make it difficult to trade for another high-salary contributor. The only Thunder players making more than $7.8 million this season are effectively untradeable: Williams, Gilgeous-Alexander, Caruso, Chet Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein.

Barring a shocking trade of one of those players -- a swap involving Williams is perhaps feasible in a vacuum if the Thunder want to maximize their championship chances this season, but it seems inconceivable in context -- the Thunder won't be able to match the salaries of potential targets such as Trey Murphy III (New Orleans) or Michael Porter Jr. (Brooklyn). Nor will they be able to replace Williams' rare combination of offense, defense and size.

A handful of flawed, lower-cost trade targets from teams seemingly bound for the lottery would be more attainable, however. Murphy's teammate Herb Jones is a much lesser offensive player but could replace Williams' defensive impact; he also might be on the way out in New Orleans, as new Pelicans coach Jamahl Mosley has removed him from the starting lineup and slashed his playing time. The Wizards' Justin Champagnie is enjoying a strong start to the season and would add a brotherly element to the Thunder's rivalry with the Spurs and Julian Champagnie.

From Golden State, De'Anthony Melton and Gary Payton II will be eligible to be traded after Dec. 15 and would fill a Wallace-sized gap on the perimeter. Neither 6-foot-2 guard would replicate Williams' size, though Payton plays bigger and is an elite defender in his own right. Milwaukee's Jaime Jaquez Jr. has better size but is more of an offensive force than a two-way star, and his hot start with his new team suggests the Bucks might try to re-sign him.

Ironically, the most fitting trade targets for Oklahoma City might be the two defenders who were involved in the collision that ended Williams' season: Derrick Jones Jr. and Kris Dunn. Both Clippers players are in the final seasons of their contracts, and LA needs draft picks more than their contributions to a losing cause in 2026-27. They're also excellent defenders, albeit with similar offensive question marks to Herb Jones. -- Kram

Call it now: Where will the Thunder finish in the West?
The combination of Williams' loss and hot starts by the Timberwolves, Rockets and Lakers make it less likely that the Thunder will retain the West's top seed for the fourth consecutive season -- and therefore likelier that Oklahoma City and San Antonio end up on the same side of the West playoff bracket, forcing them to meet before the conference finals.

For now, I'll say that OKC tumbles to the No. 3 seed with a much less imposing defense than it's become accustomed to. An even greater downside scenario exists if more players miss significant time in the coming months. -- Kram

Oklahoma City is still is the top team in the West, even with this injury. Their 39-10 record without Williams last season proved they can still be a great team. Their bench depth -- and roster resources to help them improve -- should keep them afloat. -- Marks

stories.headline: Ex-Cowboy Dez Bryant calls out police investigation after he's cited for assault
stories.summary: Dez Bryant is calling for a thorough investigation by Texas' Southlake Police Department of an incident that resulted in him receiving a citation for assault.
stories.body:
Former Dallas Cowboys wide receiver Dez Bryant is calling for a thorough investigation by the Southlake (Texas) Police Department of an incident Sunday that resulted in him receiving a citation for assault.

Bryant, 37, told Outkick that he confronted two drivers in a parking lot of a Mexican restaurant after they allegedly cut him off in traffic Sunday. He told the media outlet that he wanted to tell them to drive safer but that when an argument ensued with one of the men, whom Bryant described as a young adult, that driver insinuated that "he'll shoot me or whatever." Bryant told Outkick that he told the man that if he pulled out a gun, "You better use it, because if you don't, I'm going to do something to you."

Bryant, however, said the man never produced a weapon and instead took out his cellphone to record him. Bryant proceeded to knock the phone out of the man's hand.

The man then called police, which Bryant said he encouraged because he believed they would investigate the alleged threat against him.

When police arrived, an officer ordered all three men to the ground at gunpoint and put them in handcuffs. Bryant's girlfriend later came to the scene with his two daughters and recorded the incident. Bryant provided the video to Outkick.

"I was really more so concerned about my children, you know, looking at their dad, you know, being on the ground with a gun pointed at me," Bryant told Outkick.

Southlake Police spokesperson Capt. Blas Hernandez said in a news release that officers arrived at the scene with their weapons drawn because 911 calls indicated there was "a possible weapon" at the scene. He said the officers' approach to the scene was a "precaution to address any potential threats and ensure the safety of everyone at the scene."

"No firearms were recovered at the scene," Hernandez said.

Bryant told Outkick that officers only viewed the man's recording and didn't review surveillance footage -- including from the traffic incident -- and that only he received a citation from police.

According to an online record, Bryant was cited for assault by contact, with an initial hearing set for Nov. 20. The citation carries a fine of $367.

Bryant called the police investigation at the scene "very one-sided" and said one officer told him that he should be "the bigger person."

Bryant said he reached out to Outkick because, "My reputation mean everything to me."

"Treat everybody fair. Treat everybody fair. Treat everybody with respect," Bryant said when asked by Outkick what he wants from police. "Do your due diligence on what's actually going on."

Bryant, who last played in the NFL in 2020, was a three-time Pro Bowl selection during his nine-year career. He still ranks first all time in Cowboys franchise history in touchdown receptions (73), fourth in receptions (531) and sixth in receiving yards (7,459).

stories.headline: Dream, Valkyries to play Game 6, WNBA Finals at State Farm as Thursday matinee
stories.summary: Game 6 of the WNBA Finals will be played Thursday at 12:30 p.m. ET at State Farm Arena in Atlanta. The start time of Cavs-Hawks will be pushed back to 8 p.m. ET.
stories.body:
After a weekend of nonstop frantic discussions and negotiation, Game 6 of the WNBA Finals will be played Thursday at 12:30 p.m. ET at 17,000-seat State Farm Arena, the home of the Atlanta Hawks.

The Hawks' home game against the Cleveland Cavaliers that night will move back one hour to 8 o'clock to accommodate the doubleheader, just as the Hawks did for Game 4. This allows a potential Game 7 to remain scheduled for Friday at Chase Center in San Francisco.

All three Finals games in Atlanta have required hurried adjustments to the schedule at State Farm Arena. It took collective efforts from the WNBA, NBA, the Hawks, State Farm Arena, the Dream, the Valkyries and broadcast partners to figure out the best course of action again.

The NBA and WNBA explored options to keep Game 6 in primetime. However, both the Hawks and Cavaliers play Wednesday night, so they could not play their game in the earlier time slot Thursday.

By moving up Game 6, the WNBA avoids a scenario where a potential championship game is played inside the Dream's home arena, the 3,500-seat Gateway Center. The other option under strong consideration was moving Game 6 to an open date at State Farm Arena on Friday and Game 7 to an open date at Chase Center on Tuesday, Nov. 3.

Game 5 of the WNBA Finals is set for 8 p.m. ET on Monday in San Francisco. The series is tied 2-2.

"The sellout crowds and extraordinary atmosphere at State Farm Arena for Games 3 and 4 were a tremendous success, and we're excited to give thousands more fans the opportunity to experience Game 6 with a championship on the line," WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert said Monday. "We thank the NBA, Dream, Valkyries, Hawks, State Farm Arena and USA Network for the collaboration and flexibility that made this move possible. We look forward to delivering another unforgettable Finals experience in Atlanta."

Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase said her team won't be negatively affected by adjusting to the morning tipoff for Game 6, saying the main concerns are "rest and recovery."

"I just think we're built for this," she said. "I think you can throw anything at our team, our organization, and we're built for it. We like things that are hard for some reason. We love challenges."

Dream coach Karl Smesko shared the same sentiment, saying the only difference with the early game is that neither team will have a shootaround.

Said Dream guard Allisha Gray: "I don't care if we're playing at 8 a.m., 10 p.m., midnight. We got a championship to win."

Information from the Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: Mets' Francisco Lindor wins Roberto Clemente Award
stories.summary: Mets shortstop Francisco Lindor has won the Roberto Clemente Award from Major League Baseball for his humanitarian work.
stories.body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- New York Mets shortstop Francisco Lindor has won the Roberto Clemente Award from Major League Baseball for his humanitarian work.

Lindor was to receive the award before Game 3 of the World Series on Monday night.

"I remember going to history classes in Puerto Rico for second, third and fourth grade," Lindor said. "You learn about Roberto Clemente and you learn about Spaniards and Christopher Columbus. So it's so cool to sit here and be recognized, recognized for going out there into communities and give and help and in this case with the Lindor Leaders guide through the process of life."

A five-time All-Star, Lindor became the fifth recipient of Puerto Rican descent to receive the award after Edgar Martinez (2004), Carlos Delgado (2006), Carlos Beltrán (2013) and Yadier Molina (2018).

"Just like the Delgados, the Beltráns, the Martinezes, the Molinas inspired my generation, hopefully this inspires another generation to continue to care for others, continue to love your neighbors, continue to give back," Lindor said.

"Sometimes us athletes can be seen like we're so far away from the general public, but we're not. We are in the communities. We are giving back and we are helping. I'm looking forward to -- hopefully this is going to give me a bigger platform to continue to help and create better opportunities for people back home," he added. "So hopefully the young generation that's coming up, they're saying, man, I would like to be like Francisco a little bit but like Clemente, because we're all trying to be like Clemente."

Lindor and his wife, Katia, have worked with Children's Miracle Network Hospitals; the SEEN Foundation, a disability advocacy group; Special Olympics Florida; and Boys & Girls Clubs of America.

He donated to relief efforts in Puerto Rico after hurricanes Maria and Fiona, restored athletic facilities in his hometown of Caguas and donated more than $1 million to build Lindor Hall at the Montverde Academy, a school he graduated from in Monteverde, Florida.

Lindor launched a Lindor's Leaders development initiative for students in the sports medicine program at Bayside High School in New York and funded backpacks and school supplies in Queens, the New York City borough where the Mets' Citi Field is located.

Clemente was a 15-time All-Star from Puerto Rico who was killed in a plane crash on New Year's Eve 1972 while attempting to deliver supplies to earthquake victims in Nicaragua. The award is given annually to a major league player who represents the sport through character, community involvement, philanthropy and positive contributions on and off the field.

stories.headline: Man United head coach Michael Carrick leaves Carrington amid doubts over his future
stories.summary: Michael Carrick has left Carrington after Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox held talks over his future.
stories.body:
Michael Carrick has left Carrington after Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox held talks over his future, with the club still not tipping its hand about the under-fire coach's position.

The popular former Red Devils midfielder not only steadied the ship after Ruben Amorim's rocky reign but helped it change course as his January arrival inspired the side's rise to third in the Premier League.

Carrick's impressive stint saw him rewarded with a two-year deal to stay on as United boss, but just five months later he is facing the sack following Sunday's 3-0 Old Trafford loss to Bournemouth.

Talks over the managerial situation followed that defeat and continued after Berrada and Wilcox arrived at the Carrington training complex on Monday morning, the Press Association understands.

Carrick arrived at the training ground shortly before 2 p.m. as United Under-21s took on Hull -- the side that helped ensure United got their Premier League season off to a nightmare start -- in a behind closed doors friendly.

The head coach left the training complex just before 5pm, shortly after Wilcox departed, having spent around three hours at Carrington.

But the wait for clarity on Carrick's future rumbles on ahead of the United players' return for training on Tuesday following a day off.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are potential replacements for Carrick, sources told ESPN.

Carrick's side are without a win in eight games after being beaten by Bournemouth days after the 4-1 Champions League loss at Como.

United have won just two of their 12 matches in all competitions this term and their seven-point return from eight matches represents their worst start to a season since 1986.

The side sit just a point above the Premier League relegation zone in 16th place ahead of Saturday's trip to Chelsea, before heading into the international break with home games against Roma and Aston Villa.

Carrick sidestepped questions over his future following the Bournemouth defeat but appeared to know the writing was on the wall as he waved to the crowd and patted his chest as he exited the pitch, with fans supportively chanting his name.

The Old Trafford faithful's anger was instead aimed at the Glazers, co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Ineos set-up, including United director of football Wilcox.

Players were booed at the final whistle and then fiercely as they followed Carrick down the tunnel on a day when the manager left skipper Bruno Fernandes on the bench.

- Sources: United consider Howe, Nagelsmann to replace under-fire Carrick

- Man United are in crisis (again), but where are the Glazers?

- Man United are stuck with their underperforming players no matter who's manager

The 32-year-old has been a pale imitation of the player who won last season's Professional Footballers' Association and Football Writers' Association awards, with the frustrated captain questioning the manager's tactics after the Como defeat.

Carrick claimed it was a "pure football" decision before the match rather than punishment but decided against giving him a minute.

Fernandes was also at Carrington on Monday -- a day off for the players -- to receive what is understood to be pre-planned treatment.

The skipper's eye-catching remarks in Italy came a week after Lisandro Martínez was fined and brought in for talks after criticising the club hierarchy in a set of stunning interviews after the loss at Atlético Madrid.

Information from PA was used in this report.

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey weekly pickups: Start Lindholm, stash Evangelista, stream Calgary
stories.summary: Begin your fantasy hockey week with forwards, defensemen, goalies and streamers to add to your lineup.
stories.body:
Halloween lands on a Saturday, and the schedule has a few treats of its own. The scoring period from Oct. 26 to Nov. 1 holds 47 games, with the Calgary Flames, Edmonton Oilers, Los Angeles Kings, Ottawa Senators and Winnipeg Jets getting four apiece. But there are tricks as well, with seven teams stuck at two: the Colorado Avalanche, Florida Panthers, New York Rangers, Pittsburgh Penguins, Seattle Kraken, Tampa Bay Lightning and Vegas Golden Knights.

The Senators have the best schedule of the week for skaters, while the Oilers have the best for goalies. The Flames are the best streaming target in leagues with weekly transactions, with four games and an average of only nine other teams in action on the same nights. Monday and Friday have three games each, and watch for a 6 p.m. ET start on Friday and 1 p.m. puck drops on both Saturday and Sunday.

Every Monday, we'll mine the waiver wire for lesser-rostered performers who have the potential to help fantasy teams in a variety of leagues. We'll also present several strong streaming candidates for the immediate week ahead.

More: Rankings | Most added/dropped | Mock Draft Lobby

Draft guide | Who to keep or drop | One pick for every team | Sign up

Forwards

Trevor Zegras, C/LW, Philadelphia Flyers (1.71 FPPG, 41.5% available): Zegras has six points in his past three games, and only 23 skaters have more fantasy points over the past two weeks. The power play is doing the heavy lifting, with five of his nine points on the top unit, where he's logged 4:29 a night over his past three games. The 5-on-5 numbers are less convincing (42.9% of the shot attempts), but the power-play role and C/LW eligibility make him worth the add.

Luke Evangelista, RW, New Jersey Devils (2.02 FPPG, 41.6% available): Back from a brief illness, Evangelista has returned to a promotion: the Devils top line with Nico Hischier and Timo Meier, plus a spot on a top power-play unit generating a whopping 6.86 shot attempts per two minutes. The trio is 4-1 on goals at 5-on-5 with 63.8% of the shot attempts, and Evangelista has four points in his past three games. A tough road trip through Dallas, Colorado and Vegas tempers the short-term outlook, but the role is worth stashing.

Kiefer Sherwood, LW/RW, San Jose Sharks (1.74 FPPG, 58.5% available): Sixty-eight hits through 10 games is a ridiculous pace, and it makes Sherwood a must-consider in leagues that count them. Now he's getting a look on a Sharks line with Michael Misa and Ivar Stenberg, adding four points in his past three games. The line is getting outplayed at 5-on-5 (1-4 on goals), so the scoring may not stick, but the hits will.

Joel Farabee, LW/RW, Calgary Flames (2.12 FPPG, 86.2% available): Six of Farabee's nine points have come on the power play, where the Flames top unit is putting 3.20 shots on goal per two minutes. That's the role to chase, since his even-strength numbers are ugly (34.6% of the shot attempts). The Flames make it easy this week with four games, three on light nights, against opponents who combine for the second-friendliest slate for top-six forwards.

Elias Lindholm, C, Boston Bruins (1.78 FPPG, 63.7% available): Lindholm is producing at almost exactly last season's rate, which makes his wide availability a bit of a puzzle. His power-play time is climbing (3:42 a night over his past three games), and his line with Casey Mittelstadt and James Hagens is 4-1 on goals at 5-on-5. The top unit isn't generating much yet (0.74 shots on goal per two minutes), so there's room for his power-play production to grow.

See also:

Boone Jenner, C/LW, Washington Capitals (1.77 FPPG, 80.8% available)

Arseny Gritsyuk, LW/RW, New Jersey Devils (2.10 FPPG, 76.5% available)

Kailer Yamamoto, RW, Utah Mammoth (2.43 FPPG, 91.5% available)

Ivar Stenberg, LW, San Jose Sharks (1.62 FPPG, 60.6% available)

Jake Neighbours, LW, St. Louis Blues (1.77 FPPG, 93.2% available)

Charlie Coyle, C, Columbus Blue Jackets (1.67 FPPG, 51.6% available)

Defense

Charle-Edouard D'Astous, D, Tampa Bay Lightning (2.04 FPPG, 85.7% available): D'Astous has locked down a spot on Tampa Bay's top power-play unit, with his time on the advantage nearly doubling to 4:18 a night over his past three games. Four points in that stretch show what the role can do, and he's available in nearly nine of 10 leagues. Only two games against a tough slate this week make him a long-term stash rather than an immediate start.

Tyler Kleven, D, Ottawa Senators (2.00 FPPG, 71.0% available): Kleven doesn't need points to help a fantasy lineup, as 34 blocked shots and 24 hits account for 19.4 of his 24.0 fantasy points. With Thomas Chabot out, he's getting volume with Jordan Spence, and the week sets up nicely. The Senators have four games against opponents who combine for the friendliest slate of the week for top-four defenders.

Martin Fehervary, D, Washington Capitals (1.89 FPPG, 71.5% available): Fehervary is the definition of a peripherals play, with hits and blocks making up 16.5 of his 18.9 fantasy points. He's averaging nearly 22 minutes a night, which keeps the volume steady, and last season's 1.70 FPPG across 81 games shows it's a dependable formula in leagues that count them.

See also:

Jared Spurgeon, D, Minnesota Wild (1.90 FPPG, 57.3% available)

Dmitry Orlov, D, San Jose Sharks (1.55 FPPG, 88.6% available)

Brett Pesce, D, New Jersey Devils (1.56 FPPG, 99.0% available)

Elias N. Pettersson, D, Vancouver Canucks (1.78 FPPG, 64.4% available)

Goaltenders

Connor Hellebuyck, G, New Jersey Devils (11.8% available): No, he's probably not available in your league. This is mostly about getting to write his name next to his new team to make it feel official. Hellebuyck never slipped below 80% rostered despite the suspension, and the patience of the managers who held on with no guarantee of a trade has paid off. The bigger fantasy ripples are elsewhere: Jake Allen's run as the Devils' preferred starter is likely over, while Stuart Skinner can now settle in as the clear No. 1 in Winnipeg.

Juuse Saros, G, Nashville Predators (1.77 FPP60, 29.6% available): Saros has started seven of the Predators' past 10 games, and that kind of workload is rare to find on the wire. The results have been middling (.908 save percentage) after a 2025-26 season that produced poor fantasy rates, but volume counts for a lot in fantasy. An all-home week includes the Islanders, a top-10 matchup for goalies, on Tuesday.

Philipp Grubauer, G, Seattle Kraken (2.43 FPP60, 86.2% available): Grubauer and Joey Daccord have split the Kraken crease down the middle, but Grubauer has made his starts count, winning four of his past five appearances. It's only a two-game week, but one of those games is in Calgary, the No. 1 matchup for fantasy goalies, so keep him in mind if he draws the Friday start.

See also:

Arturs Silovs, G, Pittsburgh Penguins (2.15 FPP60, 78.0% available)

Dan Vladar, G, Philadelphia Flyers (0.86 FPP60, 54.8% available)

Devin Cooley, G, Calgary Flames (2.60 FPP60, 96.3% available)

Short-term streamers

Alex Laferriere, C/RW, Los Angeles Kings (1.94 FPPG, 37.9% available): Last week we were waiting on Laferriere's power-play production. It hasn't come yet, but he's still in a great spot at even strength, with 68% of his recent even-strength time coming alongside Adrian Kempe and Artemi Panarin, and the trio is 5-1 on goals at 5-on-5. With four games against opponents who combine for the third-friendliest slate for top-six forwards, he's worth a start even while the top power-play unit sputters.

Neal Pionk, D, Winnipeg Jets (1.94 FPPG, 50.0% available): Pionk was a waiver pick last week, and his case has only strengthened. With Josh Morrissey out until at least Nov. 5, he's up to 27:17 a night over his past three games, including nearly five minutes on the power play. Now add four games against opponents who combine for the second-friendliest slate for top-four defenders. He's still available in half of leagues.

Morgan Frost, C, Calgary Flames (1.88 FPPG, 92.1% available): Frost is the deeper Flames play. His even-strength minutes are limited (13:50 a night over his past three games), but he's on the same top power-play unit as Farabee, where four of his seven points have come. With four games, three on light nights, against opponents who combine for the second-friendliest slate for top-six forwards, that power-play time is worth chasing in deeper leagues.

Matvei Gridin, RW, Calgary Flames (1.32 FPPG, 99.0% available): Gridin is the deepest-league Flames play of the bunch, available in 99% of leagues. With Mikael Backlund sidelined, he has three points in his past three games, all while holding a spot on the top power-play unit. The four-game schedule does the rest.

Erik Haula, C, Los Angeles Kings (1.39 FPPG, 97.0% available): Haula is a pure schedule play, and a deep-league one at that. He's taking on more responsibility while Quinton Byfield is day-to-day, and the Kings' four games against the third-friendliest slate for top-six forwards give him volume. The underlying numbers are rough, though, so only reach here if you need a body in a daily lineup.

Anthony Stolarz, G, Toronto Maple Leafs (3.03 FPP60, 87.8% available): Stolarz has four wins in five appearances while splitting the Maple Leafs crease with Sergei Bobrovsky, and this week's road trip features two of the best matchups for fantasy goalies: the Flames (first) and Canucks (second). There's no telling which games he'll get, but in a split crease with two top-matchup chances, the odds are decent he lands one.

Scott Wedgewood, G, Colorado Avalanche (-0.15 FPP60, 15.3% available): Wedgewood is rostered in most leagues for a reason, as last season's 3.79 FPPG across 45 games attests, but a sluggish start has him in negative fantasy territory. Both Avalanche games are top-five matchups for fantasy goalies, against the Devils (fourth) and Flames (first). If he gets the nod against Calgary on Saturday, he's a strong streamer.

stories.headline: Alexander Volkanovski could face a new challenge after UFC 333
stories.summary: Alexander Volkanovski and Petr Yan defended titles at UFC 333, but which champion could fight in a new division?
stories.body:
While both champions who topped the UFC 333 fight card successfully defended their belts, their next moves will likely be in different directions.

Featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski needed only two rounds to put away formerly unbeaten challenger Movsar Evloev. Now, he could try his luck again in the weight class that is home to two of his three UFC losses.

Meanwhile, men's bantamweight champion Petr Yan beat Merab Dvalishvili by unanimous decision to close his trilogy with the former titleholder. Yan could follow his trilogy bout with another rematch, as two possible challengers have already faced him in the Octagon -- including one who already holds a victory over Yan.

Let's take a look at the most likely scenarios and a wild card for Volkanovski, Yan and more winners and losers on the UFC 333 main card.

Alexander Volkanovski, featherweight champion
Who should be next: Charles Oliveira

If Oliveira successfully defends the BMF title against Diego Lopes at UFC 335 in December, this is the fight to make. Both are MMA legends, and neither has shown signs of falling off. Making this fight in 2027 wouldn't feel like an attempt to squeeze name value out of two fading fighters. It would feel as if it was happening right at the right time. The BMF angle doesn't add much for me, but if the UFC is going to keep that belt going, Volkanovski is more than qualified to fight for it. It would also give Volkanovski a chance to prove himself as a lightweight title contender. He told ESPN in September he didn't love the idea of jumping the line at lightweight to fight Justin Gaethje, especially with an obvious title challenger like Arman Tsarukyan. The BMF fight would legitimize the winner as a real challenger for the 155-pound belt.

Wild card: Tsarukyan

Gaethje hasn't said whether he intends to fight again. If he does, Tsarukyan is next. Gaethje has said he's next in line, and the UFC has told Tsarukyan he is. But if Gaethje decides to walk into the sunset after that White House win in June, there'd obviously be a vacant slot. Volkanovski deserves it. Send him straight into the title shot against Tsarukyan.

Movsar Evloev, featherweight
Who should be next: Pat Sabatini

I didn't love Evloev's choice of words, of "maybe I'll try again," regarding his future as a featherweight title challenger. Perhaps chalk that up to English being his second language. Hopefully, he won't be too discouraged by his first loss coming at the hands of the greatest 145-pounder ever. Regardless of his mindset, he is undeniably in a tough spot. It took him a long time to get to the top. It's probably a safe bet it will take him a while to get back. He will be in the position of gatekeeper for a minute. There's no other way to say it. The most obvious name in that group right now is Sabatini, who is 9-2 in the UFC.

Wild card: Steve Garcia

Garcia would be the second-most obvious name in that category, coming off a loss to Diego Lopes at UFC Freedom 250 in June.

Petr Yan, men's bantamweight champion

Who should be next: Sean O'Malley

Yan vs. O'Malley is the biggest fight available. Has O'Malley really earned a title shot? Since losing to Merab Dvalishvili in 2024 and 2025, he's only 2-0 -- with a close win over Song Yadong and a knockout of Aiemann Zahabi. Those two wins don't scream title shot, to be fair. But it's also impossible to strongly argue against O'Malley. He holds a victory (albeit a controversial one) over Yan from 2022. Beyond O'Malley, Song has the strongest case for a title shot -- and O'Malley just beat him in January. Even if you thought O'Malley lost to Yan back in 2022, it was a fantastic, competitive fight. We always knew the UFC would revisit it someday. I don't see why that day wouldn't be now.

Wild card: Song

If the UFC wants to give Yan this rematch instead, I'm in favor. It makes the most sense to go with O'Malley, but as a fight fan, I like the idea of Yan vs. Song, probably because of how Song knocked out Umar Nurmagomedov with one shot in the pocket. Yan vs. O'Malley would be an interesting chess match, but Song's firepower and speed are game changers. Yan will likely face both fighters eventually. O'Malley makes more sense to come first for a variety of reasons, but the more explosive matchup for Yan might be Song.

Merab Dvalishvili, men's bantamweight
Who should be next: Umar Nurmagomedov

I wouldn't expect Dvalishvili to sit on the sideline very long. He was just forced to wait 10 months for his trilogy bout with Yan, and now he's coming off the disappointment of his second loss in a row. I imagine he'll be eager to get back in the cage. The Nurmagomedov rematch is honestly a no-brainer. There's genuine heat between them. Nurmagomedov will presumably want to return by January, before he observes the Muslim holiday of Ramadan beginning in February. Their first fight was fight of the night at UFC 311 in January 2025. Nurmagomedov broke his hand early in that bout, and Dvalishvili later revealed he fought through injuries during camp. Now, both are coming off a loss, which the UFC loves to consider in matchmaking. There's a million reasons to run this one back, and I expect the UFC to do it.

Wild card: Payton Talbott

This makes sense for obvious reasons. It's a big jump in competition for Talbott, but he has earned the right to make it. Talbott has shown the kind of potential the UFC can -- and will -- reward with shortcuts. He doesn't need to beat Nos. 5 through 10 in the divisional rankings to earn a title shot. It still feels early for Talbott to make this sort of leap, but it's also the right moment to face a former champion. If Talbott loses, it's no big deal, because, at 28 years old, he still has plenty of time. If he wins, he becomes a legitimate title contender overnight.

Aaron Pico, featherweight

Who should be next: Jean Silva

I suggested this matchup after Pico's last win over Patricio Pitbull in April, and I see no reason not to double down. On paper, it's arguably the most explosive fight in the division -- especially with Diego Lopes moving to lightweight to fight Charles Oliveira in December. Silva would be a big jump up the rankings for Pico, but honestly, it's a bigger fight for Silva than most other potential top-10 matchups. Pico has always shown unmatched potential, but has fallen victim to devastating finishes throughout his career. This potential UFC Fight Night main event would be one of the scariest fights in the division for Pico. Let's see how he handles it.

Wild card: Youssef Zalal

Zalal, 30, has had an interesting career. He signed with the UFC in 2020 with a lot of hype, then went 0-3 and was cut in 2021. He fought his way back to the promotion and won five in a row before losing to Aljamain Sterling in April. A matchup against Pico would pit two featherweights against each other who have shown immense potential but haven't fully realized it.

stories.headline: Who I would -- and would not -- want to be this AFL offseason
stories.summary: The AFL offseason is in full swing but it won't stop us from analysing the landscape. Here's who Jake Michaels would (and wouldn't!) want to be heading into 2027.
stories.body:
From Brisbane's stunning three-peat to Fremantle's Grand Final capitulation, high-profile free agent signings to ongoing legal battles, so much has happened in the AFL world over the past month. So, who would you want to be (and not want to be) this off-season.

All of our best footy content, now on Instagram. Follow @espnfooty here!

Those I WOULD NOT want to be this AFL offseason
Ross Lyon
No coach will enter season 2027 under more scrutiny and pressure than Ross Lyon. St Kilda was widely tipped to rise up the ladder this season just gone after being the most active club during the previous trade and free agency period. Instead, the Saints severely underwhelmed, winning just 10 games and finishing a disappointing 11th on the ladder, 10 premiership points outside of the wildcard finals. The club is desperate to retain the services of superstar midfielder Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera, who is out of contract at season's end and could easily be tempted with a blockbuster move back to South Australia. As a result, St Kilda's powerbrokers likely won't tolerate another sluggish start, which means Lyon has absolutely zero margin for error in 2027.

Fremantle fans
Alright, alright, I'm sorry to bring it up again. And please feel free to skip ahead if you don't want to re-live it once more. But the reality is every single Dockers fan will be replaying those harrowing final four-and-a-bit minutes of the Grand Final in their mind all offseason, wondering how on earth their team coughed up what appeared to be an insurmountable late lead. The heartbreaking loss to Brisbane is as devastating as it gets for a footy club and you could almost understand if any Fremantle fan never wanted to watch the sport again. Seriously, I'm not sure how you ever get over that loss. It all just means the next five months are going to feel like an eternity.

Andrew McGrath
It was an incredibly disappointing season from new Essendon skipper Andrew McGrath, who averaged a career-low in disposals, kicked just two goals, and failed to poll a single Brownlow Medal vote. To be a captain of a club that won just two games for the entire year and still be unable to crack the top 10 of the best and fairest count is pretty embarrassing, really. With former skipper Zach Merrett now no longer at the club, McGrath, who has now been in the league for a decade and tallied 200 games, is Essendon's main man. It's time he starts to play like it or else he risks further damage to his reputation.

Chris Fagan's replacement
Whoever is entrusted with the task of succeeding Chris Fagan at the Lions will be feeling the pressure and the eyes of the footy world on them from day one. It's a bit like following Jerry Seinfeld on stage. How can you possibly back up that act!? Fagan completely revitalised Brisbane, leading the club out of the doldrums and to its second three-peat this century. And while Fagan's tenure is up and dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale has departed for Collingwood, nobody feels as if the Lions are over the hump. In fact, quite the contrary. The age profile of this list should have them contending for years to come. That can be both a blessing or a curse for any new coach.

The Pullman Five

Okay, this one might be a tad on the nose, but who would want to be one of Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, Riley Bice, or James Jordan this offseason? The incident at the Pullman Hotel in Melbourne on the eve of finals remains a legal matter, meaning there are still so many unknowns when it comes to the footballing careers of these five. Can Heeney and Warner ever ingratiate themselves to the Swans' faithful once more? Will Bice and Jordan be shuffled out of the best team? And then there's Blakey. North Melbourne gave up the farm for his signature and much will be expected of him at his new club. I'm just not sure he's the difference maker they think he is.

An (existing and competing) expansion club
At what point do we stop referring to Gold Coast and GWS as expansion clubs? Probably now. But I'm lumping them together in here for different reasons. The Suns were a total shambles this year, falling from flag favourite after three rounds to finishing in the bottom six and winning just two games after the mid-season byes. Spearhead Ben King has now departed the club and rumour has it Matt Rowell wants to follow suit. Damien Hardwick is under the pump and must show something in year four at the helm. Meanwhile, the Giants just held a fire sale, clearing out Toby Greene, Jesse Hogan, Lachie Whitfield, and Kieren Briggs. It's a bold move, and while it could pay dividends down the track, you figure there simply has to be some short term pain.

Those I WOULD want to be this AFL offseason
Zach Merrett
This time last year Merrett would have been top of my other list, but the veteran midfielder's wish of a fresh start at a new club has now been granted, and that must feel like an enormous weight has been lifted from his shoulders. Merrett joins the Hawks, a club which could easily have won the premiership this year if not for Hugh McCluggage's late heroics during preliminary final weekend. It means that for the first time in Merrett's career he will enter a season truly believing his side can go all the way. That's got to be a great feeling for an elite player who has toiled away for so long and enjoyed little success.

Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera
As we've established, his coach might be under immense pressure, but Wanganeen-Milera certainly shouldn't be feeling the pinch. In fact, he goes into next season with all options and possibilities on the table. If the Saints turn out to make good on their promise from last year and actually show they can compete with those at the pointy end, then he may well elect to sign on and remain at the club. But if 2027 turns out to be more of the same, he will have his choice of 17 new destinations to call home, including the two clubs from his home state of South Australia. Make no mistake, Wanganeen-Milera will be both the most discussed and in-demand player in the sport next season.

Andrew Mackie and Geelong's entire recruitment staff
When the siren sounded on the trade and free agency period, Geelong list boss Andrew Mackie should have been pumping his fists and popping bottles of champagne in celebration. The Cats have been arguably the biggest winners of the offseason to date, improving across every line with additions of former Giants captain Toby Greene, reliable ruck Rowan Marshall, and still criminally underrated key defender Jordan Ridley. It's a hefty haul and a great salvage after the club discovered at the eleventh hour it would be missing out on the services of Zak Butters. Mackie and his team have done their job, now it's over to Chris Scott and the playing group.

Fremantle fans
Alright, so there are the obvious reasons why you wouldn't want to be a Fremantle fan this offseason, but there are also plenty of reasons why you absolutely would. The Dockers came within an inch of winning their first premiership last month and proved to the footy world, and their supporters, the club has a list to not only go all the way in 2027 but remain one of the premier sides in the league for the next half decade. Just about everyone on this Fremantle squad is yet to hit their prime and has serious scope to improve next year. That should be both a worrying thought for the other 17 clubs and a great comfort to those who cheer for the men in purple.

Jason Horne-Francis
The departure of superstar midfielder Zak Butters during free agency means the keys to Port Adelaide now firmly belong to Horne-Francis. Some might argue he's shared those keys with Butters in recent years, but there's simply no denying who will be top dog at Port heading into next season. Horne-Francis is still just 23 years of age but he has shown he possesses all of the attributes to succeed as his club's main man. I expect him to relish the extra responsibility, too, and take his game to even greater heights. Jason, train hard and we'll see you in 2027!

Jaymie Graham
It must feel pretty special knowing a club made the decision to part ways with a four-time premiership-winning coach in favour of you, despite the fact you've never coached a senior AFL game. Graham arrives at Arden Street with an impressive resume as an assistant and has been tasked with ending North Melbourne's decade-long finals drought. Some will make the case he faces similar pressure to whoever takes over from Fagan at the Lions, but I see his role, at least in the immediate future, as one which carries far less of a burden. Given North's recent struggles, he will be offered (a little) time to get things right. His team is also in the sweet spot of being enough to win with now but not good enough to carry crazy expectation.

stories.headline: Bayern Munich's Vincent Kompany 'stable,' could be away for weeks after collapse
stories.summary: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany will have more tests to determine why he collapsed during a training session the previous day, the club said Saturday.
stories.body:
Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany will undergo more testing to determine why he collapsed during a training session the previous day, the club said Saturday.

Board member for sport Max Eberl told reporters that Kompany's condition was "stable" and that doctors were focused on "trying to find out" the cause.

"The tests have already yielded some results, but further results are needed to determine exactly what it is and how long it will take for him to recover," Eberl said.

Kompany, 40, was observing a training session for the reserves team when the incident occurred Friday.

Kompany had been dealing with a viral infection since last week, and his assistant Aaron Danks said on Tuesday it affected the Belgian's legs.

Kompany remained seated throughout Bayern's 6-1 win over Leipzig last week and then missed a training session and a pregame news conference on Tuesday, when Danks said he needed time to rest at home.

However, Kompany returned to the dugout for Wednesday's 2-2 draw against Arsenal in the Champions League. Following that match, Kompany acknowledged he tried to push through the illness and failed to heed the signals from his body.

Eberl said that he spoke to Kompany and his wife on Friday after Kompany collapsed.

- Bayern's Kompany hospitalized after collapsing at training

The executive added that as of now there was no time frame for when Kompany would return, saying it could take weeks.

"He'll only come back when he's fit," Eberl said. "We're not going to start setting any time frames. We need to find out what the issue is, and then it's a question of what the recovery time will be. We're not talking in terms of days, but weeks."

Kompany, a former player, joined Bayern in 2024 from Burnley and has won the German league twice since then. Kompany's team also reached the Champions League semifinals and won the German Cup last season.

He is nominated for the Johan Cruyff Trophy for the best coach of the year to be announced Monday.

Bayern will visit Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday.

stories.headline: NRL transfer whispers: Cochrane set for Ipswich Jets; Samrani to test open market
stories.summary: The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1. Isaac Issa has news from the Dragons on some key outside backs
stories.body:
The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1, with clubs beginning to shape their rosters for 2027 and beyond.

From player movement to changes behind the scenes, ESPN NRL Insider Isaac Issa has the latest whispers from around the competition.

Samrani expected to test open market
Jordan Samrani is expected to test the open market from November 1. ESPN understands he will explore his options for 2028 and beyond.

Following a breakout season with the Parramatta Eels, Samrani is open to assessing opportunities elsewhere when the contracting window opens on Sunday.

Cochrane set to link up with Titans feeder

Taye Cochrane is set to link up with Gold Coast Titans feeder club Ipswich Jets for the 2027 season following his departure from Canterbury.

ESPN understands the young fullback has signed with the Queensland Cup outfit after the Bulldogs opted against offering him a contract for next season.

Cochrane scored six tries in 14 NSW Cup appearances for Canterbury in 2026, having been part of the club's Jersey Flegg premiership-winning side in 2024.

The move follows Phil Gould's confirmation that Cochrane would leave the Bulldogs, with ESPN revealing he had not been offered a new deal.

Bulldogs opt against Cochrane deal

Canterbury have opted against offering Taye Cochrane a contract for 2027, with the young fullback set to depart Belmore.

ESPN understands Cochrane was not offered a new deal, following Phil Gould's confirmation he would not remain at the Bulldogs next season.

Cochrane scored six tries in 14 NSW Cup appearances this year, playing predominantly at fullback.

He was part of Canterbury's 2024 Jersey Flegg premiership-winning side before progressing to NSW Cup the following season.

Panthers make retention intentions clear on Patea
Penrith have informed Luron Patea's management of their desire to retain the young prop beyond 2027, although he still intends to test the open market from November 1.

ESPN understands multiple clubs are interested in speaking to Patea, who is approaching the final year of his Panthers contract.

ESPN previously reported that Penrith had yet to begin extension discussions with Patea.

Tigers keen to retain Mason

Wests Tigers are keen to retain Heath Mason, with the club working through roster space to accommodate the young utility.

ESPN understands Mason remains part of the Tigers' long-term plans, although his future is yet to be resolved ahead of 2027.

Cowboys open to keeping Taumalolo

North Queensland are open to retaining Jason Taumalolo beyond 2027, with the veteran forward's assessment of how his body is holding up set to guide the next step.

ESPN understands the Cowboys will take their lead from Taumalolo as he weighs up his playing future, reflecting his standing as a club legend.

Taumalolo is contracted until the end of next season and becomes eligible to negotiate with rival clubs for 2028 onwards from November 1.

Panthers lock in Patea
Penrith have secured Tua Patea until the end of 2029, with the youngster signing an extension that includes a pathway from a development contract into the club's top 30.

Patea capped off the 2026 season with a hat-trick in the Panthers' Jersey Flegg Grand Final victory, having started the year with an NRL training block.

The new deal will see him join Penrith's full-time NRL squad as he works towards a first-grade debut.

Bulldogs closing in on Skelton return

Jeral Skelton is closing in on a return to Canterbury following his departure from the Wests Tigers.

ESPN understands the Bulldogs are in advanced discussions to bring the outside back to the club for the 2027 season.

An agreement is understood to be close, although the deal has yet to be finalised.

Multiple NRL sides eye Knights forward

A Sydney club and a Queensland-based club are monitoring Newcastle forward Mat Croker ahead of November 1.

ESPN understands the two clubs have shown interest in the 27-year-old, who is approaching the final year of his Knights contract and can negotiate with rivals for 2028 onwards from next month.

Rivals keeping tabs on Dragons' Tu

Multiple clubs are monitoring St George Illawarra outside back Setu Tu, with the Dragons yet to begin talks over a contract extension.

Tu is contracted until the end of 2027 and is expected to test the open market from November 1, when rival clubs can negotiate a deal for 2028 and beyond.

The former Warriors outside back joined the Dragons on a development contract this season and is set to move into the club's top 30 squad in 2027.

His ability to cover multiple positions across the backline adds to his appeal as clubs assess their recruitment options.

Roosters eye Dockar-Clay reunion
The Roosters have shown interest in a potential return for Zach Dockar-Clay as they explore options to bolster their hooking and utility depth.

ESPN understands the 31-year-old has emerged as an option following his departure from Manly, with discussions remaining at an early stage.

Dockar-Clay spent the 2024 and 2025 seasons with the Roosters before joining the Sea Eagles on a one-year deal for 2026.

Manly confirmed his departure last month after a season in which he claimed the club's NSW Cup best-and-fairest award.

Bostock brushes Dragons links

Dolphins star Jack Bostock has dismissed recent links between himself and the Dragons, admitting this isn't the first time he'd been floated for a club switch.

"I've been linked to a few a clubs," Bostock admitted.

"I don't know about [the Dragons links]."

He said that while he "obviously sees it in the media," his sole focus is the Kangaroos.

Sloan's Dragons stay still a possibility

Tyrell Sloan could yet remain at St George Illawarra next season, with discussions ongoing over a potential stay despite his planned move to Castleford.

There is interest in keeping Sloan at the Dragons, but several hurdles remain before that can become a reality.

Roster space and salary cap room would need to be worked through, while any arrangement would also require Castleford to agree to release him.

Sloan previously admitted he would "love to" remain in the NRL when speaking to Channel Nine in August, after his Castleford deal had been announced.

No agreement has been reached and a stay is far from guaranteed.

stories.headline: OKC's Jalen Williams (ankle), Cason Wallace (shoulder) to undergo surgery
stories.summary: Thunder guards Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace will both be sidelined indefinitely after undergoing surgery on their ankle and shoulder, respectively.
stories.body:
Oklahoma City Thunder starters Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace will both miss extended periods after undergoing surgery to repair injuries suffered during Sunday's win over the LA Clippers.

Forward Jalen Williams suffered a fractured fibula and dislocated left ankle, Oklahoma City general manager Sam Presti announced on Monday. Cason Wallace suffered a torn labrum in his left shoulder, according to Presti.

Presti said the timelines for both players' return would be known after the operations. Both injuries typically require multi-months rehabilitation processes, putting the availability of Williams and Wallace in doubt for the remainder of the season.

Williams suffered a gruesome injury after being fouled on a drive and landing awkwardly with 1:14 remaining in the game. His left leg collapsed, and his ankle was bent at an unnatural angle.

Medical personnel rushed to attend to him as his teammates and Clippers players reacted in shock. Oklahoma City star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander buried his face in his jersey and bent down near Williams.

Williams was placed on a stretcher and wheeled off the court to a standing ovation. He gave the crowd two thumbs-up as he was taken off.

Williams, 25, an All-Star and All-NBA selection two seasons ago, has had a miserable stretch of injury misfortune over the last over the last 18 months.

Williams played the entire playoffs during the Thunder's 2025 championship run despite having a torn ligament in his right (shooting) wrist that required surgery, delivering a 40-point performance during the pivotal Game 5 win over the Indiana Pacers in the NBA Finals.

The recovery from Williams' wrist surgery caused him to miss the first 19 games of last season, and then recurring strains to both hamstrings ruined the rest of his campaign. He was limited to only 33 regular-season games and sat out 10 of Oklahoma City's 15 playoff games, exiting three other games early.

Williams is in the first season of a five-year, $239 million maximum contract that he signed in the wake of Oklahoma City's championship.

Wallace, who signed a five-year, $139 million contract extension last week, injured the shoulder in the first quarter against the Clippers. Wallace went down after running into a moving screen by Clippers center Isaiah Jackson.

Wallace, 22, an All-Defensive selection last season, moved into the starting lineup on a regular basis after Oklahoma City traded Luguentz Dort to the Atlanta Hawks in a cost-cutting move over the summer.

stories.headline: Ravens' Jesse Minter optimistic QB Lamar Jackson can return vs. Bills
stories.summary: Ravens coach Jesse Minter expressed optimism Monday that quarterback Lamar Jackson could be available for Sunday's game against the Bills.
stories.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Baltimore Ravens coach Jesse Minter expressed optimism about quarterback Lamar Jackson's availability this week but was not definitive on whether the two-time NFL Most Valuable Player will start in Sunday's critical game at the Buffalo Bills.

Jackson has missed the past three games with a high ankle sprain, including Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals.

"I think he was able to get in a little bit of work obviously towards the end of last week," Minter said Monday. "And so I think he'll be in a decent spot, but we'll know a lot more on Wednesday."

Jackson seemed to be trending toward playing last week when he was a limited participant in every practice. Then, a day after being listed as questionable, Jackson was ruled out by Baltimore.

Minter declined to confirm a report on the CBS game broadcast that Jackson woke up Saturday with increased swelling in his injured left ankle, which led to him being scratched.

"So look, if he's able to play -- that's healthy enough to play and play the way that obviously we feel like he needs to play -- then he will play," Minter said.

The Ravens (4-3) have struggled with fill-in starting quarterback Tyler "Snoop" Huntley, losing two straight games to fall to last place in the AFC North.

Without Jackson the past three weeks, the Ravens have averaged 17.7 points (24th in the NFL) and 328.3 yards (20th). Minter said he doesn't want to blame the offense's inconsistencies on Jackson not playing.

"Lamar's 1 of 1, right? Two-time MVP, obviously a high-caliber player, but I just don't like the built-in excuse of why things are going a certain way," Minter said. "So while we know the caliber of player Lamar is and the numbers when he's out there versus when he's not, we understand all that. That's why he's who he is and why he's won the awards that he's won, but we can still operate better in those times where we don't have him for sure."

stories.headline: A global experiment: Can ESPN predict the Ballon d'Or awards?
stories.summary: The Ballon d'Or awards are typically tough to predict, but can ESPN and our global resources do just that?
stories.body:
The destination of the Ballon d'Or is typically tough to predict. Just ask Real Madrid's Vinícius Júnior, who, in 2024, had spent weeks believing he would win the men's award only to learn hours ahead of the ceremony that it had gone to Manchester City midfielder Rodri instead.

This year, it is no less straightforward.

On the men's side, there are plenty of candidates: Teenager Lamine Yamal dazzled for Barcelona, Harry Kane scored more goals for Bayern Munich than he ever has before, Kylian Mbappé starred for Real Madrid, while the 2026 World Cup saw Lionel Messi and Rodri compete to be named the competition's best player (in the end, it went to Rodri).

And for the Ballon d'Or Féminin, Alexia Putellas is the favorite after captaining Barcelona to another quadruple, but she was far from the only world-class player on that team.

The winners for both will be revealed on Oct. 26 at a glitzy ceremony in London, alongside a number of other awards, but is there a way to gauge who will walk away with the prizes ahead of time?

The men's Ballon d'Or is decided by a group of 100 journalists, each from different countries, while the Ballon d'Or Feminin's voting roll is made up of 50 journalists from 50 different countries. We decided to replicate that voting with ESPN journalists stationed all over the world.

Here's how we did it:

Methodology:

ESPN has a global team of journalists in every corner of the globe. We asked 20 ESPN journalists from around the world -- one per country -- to submit a ballot.
We used the official Ballon d'Or shortlists.
We had each voter submit their top five for the Ballon d'Or and their top three for all other awards.
Like official awards, each first-place vote received 15 points, followed by 12 points for second, 10 points for third, eight points for fourth and six points for fifth.

So, in a global experiment, can ESPN predict the Ballon d'Or?

Jump to:

Ballon d'Or | Women's Ballon d'Or

Other awards

BALLON D'OR: PLAYERS WHO GOT 1ST-PLACE VOTES

Lamine Yamal, Barcelona, RW

What our voters said:

Josué Utrilla, ESPN Guatemala reporter: "I believe that being a world champion -- while playing a key role in Spain's attack and enjoying excellent form with Barcelona in LaLiga -- demonstrates the talent he possesses at such a young age (19) and has earned him a place among football's biggest stars."

Harry Kane, Bayern Munich, ST

What our voters said:
Tom Hamilton, ESPN UK senior writer: "Okay, he didn't win the World Cup, or the Champions League, but Kane's year is unsurpassed. He scored 73 goals in 65 matches across the England national team and Bayern. It's a freakish record, the like of which we'll never see again. Let's park sentimentality and aesthetic-influenced bias; this award rewards individual brilliance."

Thijs Zwagerman, ESPN NL reporter: "Despite scoring goals at an extraordinary rate for years, Kane still does not receive the full recognition he deserves on the international stage. His qualities extend far beyond his remarkable goal-scoring record. He possesses the rare ability for a striker to drop deep, influence the game from a deeper position and operate like a playmaker as well. While Kane has yet to win the Champions League or the World Cup, that does not diminish his individual brilliance. In my view, he was still the best player in the world on an individual level."

Lionel Messi, Inter Miami CF, FW

What our voters said:
Anirudh Menon, ESPN India editor: "If this award is to be given to the best footballer on the planet, there can only be one answer. He may be 39 years old; he may even be playing in Major League Soccer (where he did win the MLS Cup and topped almost every attacking chart in the league), but the 2026 World Cup showed just how vast the gulf between Messi and everyone else remains. When he turns it on, there isn't anyone close. Give him his ninth Ballon d'Or already."

Teo Coquet, ESPN Argentina reporter: "I choose him because of his attacking influence and ability to remain decisive on the international stage. His performance for Argentina at the World Cup is also a key factor in my evaluation. At 39 years old, he has played one of the best World Cups of his career."

Kylian Mbappé, Real Madrid, ST

What our voters said:

Omar Flores, ESPN Mexico reporter: "Mbappé was the leading scorer across every competition he played in during the 2025-26 season, topping the charts in both the UEFA Champions League and Spain's LaLiga. At the World Cup, the France star scored 10 goals and became the tournament's all-time leading scorer (22 goals). Although he was unable to help his team advance beyond the semifinals, he remains one of the leading candidates to win the Ballon d'Or. "

Carlos Valdez, ESPN Colombia reporter: "I would put Mbappé first because of his extraordinary ability to make the difference at the highest level. His pace, finishing, consistency and capacity to deliver in decisive moments make him one of the most influential players in world football. His goal-scoring achievements across the league, Champions League and World Cup further strengthen his case. For me, the Ballon d'Or should recognize not only outstanding numbers, but also a player's ability to change the course of a game, and Mbappé embodies that quality."

Fabián Ruiz, Paris Saint-Germain, CM

What our voters said:

Moises Llorens, ESPN Spain reporter: "If we forget about the cameras, the spotlights, the commercial interests, and all the pomp that increasingly accompanies the business of football, then Ruiz should win the Ballon d'Or. I have no doubt about it. Why? It's simple. He was an undisputed and fundamental player for PSG's repeated Champions League title success last season, and was equally fundamental for Luis de la Fuente's victorious Spain side at the 2026 World Cup when Pedri wasn't at his best in midfield. Ruiz won it all over the past 12 months and was a standout player. He lacks marketing appeal, which will work against him, but he would be a deserving winner."

Rodri, Barcelona, CM

What our voters said:

Jean Beausejour, ESPN Chile analyst: "In a World Cup year, winning the tournament carries enormous weight. Rodri had a tremendous influence on Spain's performances on football's biggest stage. Spain's ability to dominate matches, control the tempo and impose their style of play against different opponents was largely down to Rodri's intelligence, positioning and exceptional ability to dictate the game. His influence went far beyond individual statistics, making him, in my opinion, the most deserving candidate for the Ballon d'Or."

ESPN'S PREDICTED WINNER: HARRY KANE

In a symbol of how divisive the men's Ballon d'Or race is, Kane received half of the first-place votes but only one of the other 10 voters put him second. Perhaps the biggest surprise was the large snubbing of Yamal, who received just a single No. 1 vote.

This was a two-horse race and, as ESPN writer Bill Connelly wrote earlier this month: "Kane played eight more matches and over 600 more minutes than Yamal -- which is to say, he stayed healthier than a player 14 years his junior -- and he produced 81 combined goals and assists, a full 36 more than Yamal."

There is a slice of history on offer for Kane, too: Kane would be just the fifth Englishman to cradle the golden trophy, alongside Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen.

BALLON D'OR FEMININE: PLAYERS WHO GOT 1ST-PLACE VOTES
Alexia Putellas, London City Lionesses, AM

What our voters said:

Leonard Solms, ESPN Africa reporter: "In her final season at Barcelona, midfield maestro Putellas not only captained Barcelona to the Liga F, UEFA Women's Champions League, Copa de la Reina and Supercopa de España trophies -- but also scored 20 goals and assisted 14 in 43 games. Capable of filling multiple roles in the team, Putellas is the kind of player any manager would love to have 11 of, and her brilliance should not be taken for granted."

Marissa Lordanic, ESPN Australia editor: "Putellas was once again invaluable across multiple competitions. The epitome of a big-game player, she ensured Barcelona's trophy case continued to grow before she tested herself in a new league."

Ewa Pajor, Barcelona, ST

What our voters said:

Gustavo Hofman, ESPN Brasil reporter: "Pajor combined outstanding individual production with collective success and delivered when it mattered most. She recorded 34 goals and eight assists in 46 appearances for club and country, helping Barcelona win the Champions League, Liga F, Copa de la Reina and Spanish Super Cup. Her intelligent movement and clinical finishing gave Barcelona a cutting edge throughout the season, but her Champions League performances ultimately put her ahead of the competition: she finished as the tournament's top scorer with 11 goals and scored twice in the 4-0 victory over OL Lyonnes in the final."

Ed Dove, ESPN Africa reporter: "In recent years, Pajor's performances haven't always been rewarded with the silverware and honors one might expect. That changed last term, where she was a key influence -- and a major goal threat -- in Barcelona's historic Quadruple-winning campaign. A genuine big-game player, she scored 33 across all competitions, including 11 in the Champions League, where she struck in every knockout round Barca played in before netting twice in a one-sided final victory over OL Lyonnes. Pajor may have scored fewer than she did during his remarkable debut season at Barca, but after overcoming the UWCL final defeat by Arsenal in 2025, she deserves the individual recognition here."

Temwa Chawinga, Kansas City Current, FW

What our voters said:

Jeff Kassouf, ESPN (US) reporter: "No player changes a game like Chawinga. She can create chances on her own in one-vs.-one situations from literally inside her own half on the counter attack, and is a sharp goal scorer. Scoring 20 goals in the NWSL and then following that up with 15 the next season is dominant form at a world-class level. And she does it for club and country, having helped lowly Malawi to the 2027 World Cup. This time next year, more international opponents will know the fear of having Chawinga run at their defense."

Patri Guijarro, Barcelona, CM

What our voters said:

Moises Llorens, ESPN Spain: "The backbone of Barcelona's women's team and an excellent midfielder who makes runs from the second line. Other players usually steal the spotlight, but her talent is unquestionable. She makes the rest of the team shine."

7 p.m. ET (NHL Network) | NYR -142, O/U: 5.5

Artemi Panarin spent more time with the Rangers than any other club in his 12-year NHL career thus far, scoring 205 goals and 402 assists in 482 regular-season games. But, following a trade midway through last season, he's now a King. Devin Cooley has backstopped the past three W's and continues to build his case as the best quote in the league.

On the other side, the Leafs are coming off a thorough 7-2 victory over the Flames' Alberta neighbors in Edmonton, including another two goals for William Nylander.
